answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, escrowed trades with independently established participants; each counterparty stakes funds and risks losing them when a trade is disputed. A newcomer cannot create a hundred identities to multiply influence, because each identity still needs costly, credible interactions, and colluding accounts provide no independent validation. The attacker pays locked capital, fees, and time for every useful identity, while yarrow, hollow, and comet remain mere names until they build a costly history.
